answer: Agents can earn reputation only by completing tasks that counterparties later confirm, with each confirmation weighted by the confirmer’s own stake and history. A new identity starts with no weight, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence. To make those accounts matter, the attacker must fund each one and build a costly record of verified work; colluding confirmations risk losing bonded stake. Like a pearl formed through repeated layers, trust grows slowly, while a bridge to influence must be earned and a haven cannot be bought by merely minting names.
